newsitem.title: USA: US ag attache cuts 96/7 Argentina soybean forecast.
newsitem.headline: US ag attache cuts 96/7 Argentina soybean forecast.

text.p: An agricultural attache at the American embassy in Buenos Aires lowered his forecast for the 1996/97 Argentina soybean crop to 11.5 million tonnes from 12.4 million tonnes, citing damage from prolonged drought.

"Nearly final harvest results have demonstrated the damage caused to soybeans by the prolonged drought centered in Santa Fe and Cordoba provinces..." the attache wrote in a report dated June 4 that was released in Washington on Monday.
The attache also said sharp downfall in estimated production as compared to earlier in the year would leave less product available for all uses.

He said the crushing industry was expected to be more aggressive in purchasing local and imported product to continue their operations, but overall availability will result in less crush than earlier estimated.
"According to trade sources, purchases of soybeans have been made from Bolivia, Paraguay and most recently, the United States, and total about 150,000-200,000 (tonnes)," the attache wrote.

He said although there is some export business taking place, it is significantly slower as compared to last year, while purchases by the local crushing industry are over 3.0 million tonnes, over 1.0 million tonnes greater than at the same date last year.

Attache reports are not official USDA data. In its last World Supply and Demand Report issued May 12, USDA pegged Argentina 1996/97 soybean production at 12.4 million tonnes. The department will release its next report on June 12.
